notes.title: Character Spotlight: The Preacher
notes.content:
[p]Sometimes the battlefield needs more than bullets and bravado, it needs a soothing (or debilitating) presence. Enter the [b]Preacher[/b], a close-range ranged fighter (yes, that’s a thing) who specializes in breaking enemy morale while keeping your crew in the fight.[/p][p]This class doesn’t dominate with raw damage but with control, by weakening enemies, soothing allies, and throwing curses that can tilt entire encounters in your favor.  

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45257520/278a51e391975f121087fb8e320deaafe7d46005.jpg"][/img]
 SKILLS  [/p][p][b]Affront[/b][/p][p]Forget polite disagreements, this is a straight-up smack-down to an enemy’s confidence. Use it to strip away their power, dodge and movement speed, turning a dangerous foe into an easy target. Perfect for softening up elites or keeping a heavy hitter from reaching your lines.[/p][p][b]Soothing Words[/b][/p][p]For a class that throws so much shade, the Preacher also knows how to lift spirits. Mark an ally with a Sacred Echo, and with just the right timing, you’ll restore their health when they need it most. It’s subtle-ish (at 8 hp), but in a long fight, that healing can mean the difference between victory and a crew-sized funeral. [b] 

Caravan Skill: Curse[/b][/p][p]Placed in the backline, the Preacher brings out the big guns (metaphorically speaking). Curse is a map-wide debuff that saps enemy strength and mobility, letting your frontline dismantle them while they struggle to keep up. It’s like putting the entire enemy squad in quicksand.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45257520/a5f291482dc7b2c8dbb33b677fa3bd95c2ad0e0f.jpg"][/img]

🛠️ [b]Designer’s Note – Tasos[/b]:
 The Preacher is the only class with an innate healing ability, and pairing that with their nasty debuffs makes them an absolute gem for longer runs. Personally, I love having one in the party because they do double duty—protecting your team while dismantling the enemy’s momentum.[/p][p]Bring a Preacher along if you want your enemies humbled and your allies kept alive long enough to celebrate their victory.[/p]

notes.title: Character Spotlight: The Sniper
notes.content:
[p]Sometimes the best defense is eliminating someone before they even get a turn.
Enter: the Sniper. Precise, patient, and downright deadly.[/p][p]This class isn’t about spraying bullets or holding the line—it’s about picking your moment and making it count. The Sniper shines brightest when they’ve got space to work with and a juicy target lined up. One clean shot can change the course of a fight.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45257520/c803c7653db2e9cb61467906f1f419adb772d686.png"][/img]
SKILLS
[b]Aim. Breathe. Squeeze.[/b]
It’s not just a mantra—it’s your enemy’s worst nightmare. This ability does exactly what you think it does: high damage, long range, no mercy.
If you see an elite enemy or a healer in the backline, don’t wait. Just pull the trigger and watch them crumble.[/p][p][b]Steady Aim[/b]
Why rush? This ability gives you the clarity you need to [i]really[/i] make the next shot hurt, at the cost of -1 AP.
Use it to gain a precision buff, boosting your next attack for even higher damage. Time it well and you’ll delete a target in one turn, guaranteed.
[b]
Caravan Skill: Longshot[/b]
When your Sniper is chilling in the back of the caravan, they’re not wasting time—they’re lining up a monster shot.
[b]Longshot[/b] is a devastating, single-target caravan skill that reaches across the battlefield to remove a high-value threat. Low cooldown, massive payoff.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45257520/a6651ac1d70619dc19348a62ce1410902132681c.png"][/img]

🛠️ [b]Designer’s Note – Tasos[/b]:[/p][p]The Sniper is our favorite assassin. Cold, quiet, and incredibly effective at thinning out enemy ranks before things get messy.[/p][p]If you like having surgical answers to big problems, this is the class for you. Nothing feels quite as good as watching that health bar vanish in a single shot.

Keep one eye on the battlefield and one finger on the trigger.[/p][p]The Sniper’s always watching—just hope they’re on your side.[/p]

notes.title: Character Spotlight: The Support
notes.content:
Don’t let the name fool you—Support isn’t here just to hand out water and psychological encouragement. This versatile class controls the battlefield like a boss!

With a knack for locking down space and buffing teammates at key moments, the Support doesn’t just assist—they set the pace, draw the lines, and in case you need that extra firepower is there to add some ranged damage for good measure.

[h2]Skills[/h2] 
[b]Minefield[/b]
Nothing screams “you shall not pass” like a freshly dropped minefield. Unless someone passes over it, in which case you can put on your sunglasses and deliver a punchy one liner.
Whether it’s cutting off flanking routes, protecting your squishier crew, or forcing enemies down a very painful hallway, this ability turns positioning into a win condition.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45257520/9d374d88e3b879a36098074c36168a45751673a3.jpg[/img]

The Minefield is a draw skill, meaning you can hold your mouse over the grid until you have covered the area you want. After that you can focus on your positioning or any other objectives, having your bases covered! 
Disregard that I am trapping someones drying laundry in the picture above.

[b]Rile Up[/b]
Give your team the hype they need—a powerful buff that turns your next turn into a highlight reel. Time it right and you’ll see your crew explode with power, wiping the field before the enemy even knows what happened.
While the added Critical could possibly one-shot an adversary, the flat Power boost alone is worth it, especially when the buff is active for two turns. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45257520/cbbd1238beb25b7e5866dbbde82d39beb11f98d4.jpg[/img]

Simply place the area over your crew and get ready for some serious damage, like it's no one's business! 

[b]Caravan Skill: Sharpen Senses[/b]
A crew that sees it coming is a crew that lives to tell the tale. Placing the Support on the back-line of your Caravan will unlock this powerful buff during combat for your front-liners. 
This team-wide buff massively boosts your dodge chance when it matters most. [strike]You might not always need it, but when you do..[/strike]—Trust me this is awesome, it’s a run-saver. 

    🛠️ Designer’s Note - Tasos: [i]The Support is one of those classes that just makes everything better. Lay down some mines, rile up your heavy hitters, and let the rest of the team follow your tempo. Whether you’re funneling enemies into traps or setting up a huge combo turn, this class is a tactical backbone.[/i]

So consider having a Support on your next run! Bring one along if you like winning!

notes.title: Character Spotlight: The Marine
notes.content:
Sometimes you don’t need a sniper or a hammer-swinging maniac. Sometimes you just need a Marine—reliable, tactical, and always ready to control the flow of combat with a grin.

This gun-wielding class brings mid-range firepower, mid-health durability, and enough crowd control to make you feel like you’re always one step ahead. The Marine won’t top the damage charts, but in the right hands? Oh, they’ll win you the fight.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45257520/837e7eebc827bf0b5b0f4bfecf868a235c2d44a5.png[/img]

[h2]Skills[/h2] 
[b]Displacement Shot[/b]
It’s not just for laughs—this skill pushes enemies back, and if they hit something on the way (like a wall... or one of your Fire Pillars 👀), they take extra damage. It’s a positioning tool and a bonus damage dealer in one clean shot.

[b]Flashbang[/b]
This one’s for those crowded brawls—Area of Effect blind that makes enemies miss more. Works wonders when you’re surrounded or just want to give your brawlers a bit of breathing room.

[b]Caravan Skill: Spray and Pray[/b]
When you absolutely, positively need everything in front of you deleted—call in this AOE caravan attack. It’s not subtle, but it doesn’t have to be.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45257520/1ef6884fecb635629760d5489312d7e5670412a5.png[/img]

🛠️ Designer’s Note - Tasos : [i]This one’s a personal favorite. The Displacement Shot → Fire Pillar combo is chef’s kiss—tactical, satisfying, and incredibly effective.[/i]

Whether you're pushing enemies into traps or blinding them before the real fight starts, the Marine has your back. Keep one in your squad—you’ll thank yourself later.

notes.title: 4 Combat Tips to Keep You (and Your Crew) Alive
notes.content:
So you’ve just stepped into the scorching sands, your ship’s barely holding together, and an angry Arcanist warband is charging your way—what now?

Combat in Dunebound Tactics isn’t about who has the biggest hammer/gun/staff (though, fair, some are very big), it’s about knowing when to strike, where to stand, and how to make every skill count. Here’s a quick rundown of 4 combat tips to help you survive your next firefight, ambush, or “oops this was supposed to be a peaceful negotiation” moment.

[h2]1. Prep Like a Pro[/h2]

The real fight starts before you enter combat.

Before the first rock gets thrown or explosive pillar gets summoned, ask yourself: does my squad actually work well together?

Build your crew with synergy in mind. A healer in your team can be the difference between limping into the Medbay or walking out with a smirk and full HP. Support characters with buffs, crowd control, or combo synergy can turn a desperate scrap into a clean sweep. Think of your team like a toolbox—if you only pack hammers, don’t be surprised when screws get the better of you.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45257520/a1d01e24d04393dfed9f10b1bebd4a99afe10807.png[/img]

[h2]2. Read the Room (and the Rocks)[/h2]

Not every battle is a punch-up.

Sometimes you’re defending an NPC. Sometimes you’re being picked apart by ranged enemies. Sometimes, it’s a full-on brawl in a dense cityscape. So your positioning needs to change with the situation.

Got melee enemies charging you? Get behind cover or funnel them into tight spaces. Need to protect someone important? Send your toughest fighter to body-block the heat. Don’t just charge in—adapt your formation to the field.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45257520/07349672e6221745180953c0504a8d2791294ec2.png[/img]

[h2]3. Draw Skills = Big Brain Plays[/h2]

Despite the name, Draw skills aren’t about pulling enemies—they’re about placement.

Using your mouse, you’ll “draw” the layout of things like clusters of pillars, mines, or explosive lines, giving you the power to reshape the battlefield on your terms. Block a chokepoint. Cover your flank. Create a deadly trap that detonates the moment an enemy moves.

These skills are versatile and creative—so go wild with your layouts. One smart Draw can save your whole crew (or blow up half the enemy squad in one go).

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45257520/9b568ae66ad43ea3757416db44d838720176fe4a.png[/img]

[h2]4. Backline Brilliance[/h2]

Backline skills hit like a sandstorm when used right—and yes, they do cost Elios to activate. That might feel steep at first (especially when you're watching your fuel reserves like a hawk), but hear us out.

Most of these abilities are AoE, meaning they can wipe out clusters of enemies, reshape terrain, buff your whole squad, or swing a losing battle in your favor in one clean strike. And if you don’t use them? You might end up eating more damage, which means spending even more Elios later in the Medbay—or worse, losing a crew member entirely... which also means losing their Elios.

So weigh your options, but don’t be stingy when your backline has the power to tip the scales.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45257520/71dd7dacc002f399b9e468dc295008880a20ac80.png[/img]

Combat in Dunebound Tactics isn’t just a numbers game. It’s a puzzle, a dance, and sometimes a straight-up brawl. Hopefully, these tips give you the edge the next time things go sideways.

Now go raise some dust. And maybe a few explosive pillars while you're at it.

notes.title: Running on fumes? Tips for Elios Management!
notes.content:
So, you’ve set off into the endless sands, caravan creaks under your heels, and suddenly—oh no—you’re out of Elios. No fuel, no movement. No movement… well, RIP.

Before we dive into survival tips, let’s talk about what makes Elios so special. 

[h3]What is Elios?[/h3]
It’s not just fuel—it’s a[b] triple-point state of matter[/b], existing as a solid, liquid, and gas all at once. This strange, ever-shifting nature makes it incredibly powerful but also highly unstable. If not collected in time, it seeps back into the environment, lost forever. 

And since your entire journey depends on keeping a steady supply, knowing how to manage Elios is the difference between survival and becoming another wreck buried in the dunes.

On that note: 

[h3]Stick Around for that sweet, sweet Elios[/h3]
When enemies die, they don’t just leave behind loot—they release Elios fields. Standing around the statue of your former adversary you can collect a whole bunch of it. 

If you want to be cheeky, you can bait two enemies next to one another and gather double the Elios per turn- by positioning your crew-mate at the overlapping space of the fields!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45257520/bb3eb61025c13e5a8bce8fb8dd85785e02ca0674.jpg[/img]

Just remember: If you rush off too soon, that [b]energy disperses into the sands[/b]. Stay put, soak it up, and make sure your ship keeps running.

[h3]Medbay Is Nice… but Pricey[/h3]
Healing is great, but here’s the catch: the [b]Medbay runs on Elios[/b]. You’re literally burning your fuel to patch up your crew. 

Sometimes that’s worth it, but other times? Maybe just walk it off. A bruised fighter is better than a dead caravan stranded in the dunes.

Keep in mind that, when used, each slot multiplies your consumption by distance traveled. Don't get me wrong, its a useful tool, but sometimes the "all for one" approach instead of the "one for all" strategy is risky.  

[h3]…Or You Could Just, You Know, "Repurpose" Your Crew[/h3]
Hard truth time—your crew is also made of Elios. [b]Every last one of them[/b]. 

Look, tough choices have to be made in the wasteland. If you’re desperate, your crew technically counts as a walking, talking fuel source.

If you’re desperate, you can extract that precious energy from their bodies, turning them into fuel for the caravan. That breaks them in the process, but they are technically alive (the first time you convert them). Sure, it’s a bit grim, but out here, survival isn’t pretty. Besides, would they rather walk through the desert? No? Thought so.

[h3]The Last Stand – A Final, Desperate Fight[/h3]
When all else fails, when your Elios reserves are dry, and the sands have turned against you, there’s only one option left—Last Stand.

This isn’t just another fight; it’s a desperate, all-or-nothing battle where every single member of your caravan takes up arms. Enemies will swarm from all sides, and survival is far from guaranteed. But if you manage to claw your way through, you’ll earn one final burst of Elios—just enough to push forward.

There’s no cheesing this, no spamming it for easy fuel. It’s a [b]one-time deal per run[/b], so use it wisely. If you trigger it too soon, you might not have the strength to survive. Too late, and, well… the desert doesn’t leave second chances.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45257520/6d1b1f8f2b66ed5cdfa73aca6fb88eb5d5da3145.jpg[/img]
[b]And there you have it![/b] 
Manage your fuel wisely, make the hard calls when needed, and keep that caravan moving at all costs! Got a better way to stockpile Elios? Share your wisdom—we promise we won’t judge… much.

notes.title: Gameplay Rundown part 2/2- Combat and beyond
notes.content:
[u][b]Combat[/b][/u]
Sooner or later, you’ll face your enemies in battle. 
The Frontline will step up to the challenge—hopefully surviving to tell the tale.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45257520/9226e92a7623f858f01d96e4099fa6220e007773.png[/img]
Each battlefield presents unique challenges, and every scenario shifts the rules. Walking into a fight is a bold act of defiance, with ripple effects that will shape your run.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45257520/abdc12f78250e20e891169b2e2660f86fe4fcd03.png[/img]
Combat is dynamic, with terrain playing a crucial role. Some characters can reshape it entirely, like creating stone pillars to block paths or explosive ones to set traps. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45257520/82eef93d7086e659fdcbd92bdeb3e1dc934bde0f.png[/img]
Most characters can destroy terrain pieces like rocks, houses, or boxes—sometimes with nothing but their own head, a bullrush!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45257520/4ee3415ba3cc8f40d560427a366b7e209041e566.png[/img]
Amid the chaos, you can harvest Elios from fallen enemies—or even allies—by staying near their petrified remains. Just be careful: standing still might make you the next target.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45257520/0415df6f9ac853d9cc9f2651ca98fa1e2a55de98.png[/img]
Combat is the epitome of chaos throughout history, and it’s up to you to keep a cool head. Plan each move with precision and purpose, or risk watching your run come to an untimely end.

[u][b]The Great Beyond[/b][/u]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45257520/b5295905a989f7c50a612b039987da6d3a27aec9.png[/img]
In the trailer’s final moments, a great mechanical hand rises, holding an island with a lighthouse-like tower and a pure sphere of Elios at its peak.
Is it a beacon of hope? Or the lifeforce of crews who came before you?
You WILL find out..


Thanks so much for reading! We’ll return soon with more Dunebound Tactics stories. Let us know what you think—we’d love to hear from you!

notes.title: Gameplay Rundown- Starting, Roles, Events
notes.content:
You wake up one morning and—BAM!
[b]Dunebound Tactics[/b] is announced, and the trailer drops a [i]metric ton[/i] of gameplay straight onto your unsuspecting eyeballs!
Here’s a basic rundown of the mechanics revealed in the trailer for Terahard’s Roguelite, Turn-Based RPG.

[u][b]Starting off[/b][/u]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45257520/ef7f5f9167f2a1119979f1007184a7f9b752cfd4.png[/img]
The Mechanic welcomes you into his shop, and since he’s quite the talkative fellow, you can ask him about the world, his life, or details about the island.
He’s even polite enough to ask about [i]your[/i] motivations for this run. Your answer will affect the party, so take a moment to consider your response carefully.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45257520/31e6727b663b3bc7cf1488e6e54a903e0b237fb3.png[/img]
Next, you can head to the local tavern, where new characters can be recruited—for a price.
Each recruit has their own class and unique trait, so look for synergies that complement your playstyle or round out your party composition.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45257520/27c91cfb9748f0ffeb41ac7199400f41a7302e79.png[/img]
You can choose to spend some of your starting Elios here—or not. The choice is yours.
Feeling ruthless? You could even turn one or more members of your crew into Elios to recruit someone more suitable. Or you could let the patrons alone, leaving them to carve their own path through the desert.
Some advanced structures teased in the trailer might require their own deep dive (spoilers, anyone?), but for now, let’s follow the Ley Lines!

[u][b]Roles[/b][/u]
Your crew can take on distinct roles aboard the Caravan, as seen on the bar to the left:
[b]The Frontline[/b] – Faces combat and handles dangerous events head-on.
[b]The Backline[/b] – Supports the Frontline, during combat, with skills from atop the Caravan.
[b]The Medbay[/b] – Where the Frontline will likely end up after a fight.
You can rearrange your party while crossing the desert to best prepare for your next destination.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45257520/62fb91c07bffcbeb6a77dd5b4e2a2eeaae81305c.png[/img]
But Remember: your engine requires Elios to keep the Caravan moving. Run out, and you’ll be forced to make some [i]very[/i] difficult choices.

[u][b]Events[/b][/u]
Scattered across the desert, events are marked with a three-dot icon. Each event presents a choice with varied outcomes.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45257520/fca277a0488e20ff12e8ea7b30426436bc8d5f20.png[/img]
Will you:
Shelter an Imperial Traitor to gain Elios?
Run them over because of their past crimes?
Or pass them by, wary of a possible ambush?
Events can grant buffs, wounds, extra Elios, new teammates, or even debuffs. The ever-shifting sands ensure that anything is possible.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45257520/c1f939c61b467a093db175d2c2e55e8b9554e16a.png[/img]
Some choices require specific characters, classes, or skills to unlock alternative options. As always, it pays to come prepared.

Thanks so much for reading! 
We’ll return soon with more Dunebound Tactics stories, namely the combat. 
Let us know what you think—we’d love to hear from you!

notes.title: 4000 Thank You!
notes.content:
We were simply blown away by the community’s response to the announcement of our game! 
We are proud to announce that Dunebound Tactics has gathered more than 4000 wishlists in less than a week! 

This means so much to us, and has given us so much energy to make the best game that we possibly can, as we continue working towards the release (with a couple of fun surprises along the way, for good measure)! 


Aris Tsevrenis, Terahard’s sand-ship captain, when asked on the “why” of Dunebound Tactics had the following to say: 
"Personally, I'm a huge tactics fanatic. We built our very own tactics engine with RPG elements from the ground up for Dunebound Tactics! I'm excited both for the technical innovations as well as the freedom we gave our game designers to create an amazing experience. The art in this game is the best we've managed so far connecting all the little details to squeeze performance and quality."

The announcement was picked up by the media as well, and we would like to send our thanks to IGN, Rock Paper Shotgun, TurnBased Lovers and TechPowerUp, just to name a few. You can read the articles below!  

[url=]https://www.ign.com/videos/dunebound-tactics-official-announcement-trailer[/url]

[url=]https://www.rockpapershotgun.com/dunebound-tactics-brings-terrain-manipulation-to-a-strategy-rpg-where-you-can-sacrifice-companions-to-power-your-ship[/url]

[url=]https://turnbasedlovers.com/news/tactical-roguelite-dunebound-tactics-announced/[/url]

[url=]https://www.techpowerup.com/327820/dunebound-tactics-kicks-up-the-dust-with-its-steam-page-launch-and-a-first-trailer[/url]

Last but not least, we would like to thank each and everyone of you, for making the announcement of our new game special! It means the world to us! If you have any questions, suggestions and anything in between, hit us up and we might even do a full piece on them!

New updates, deep dives on the mechanics and art of the game are coming soon, so stay tuned for more! 

Cheers!

notes.title: Announcing Dunebound Tactics!
notes.content:
Hello everyone! 
We are excited to announce our latest project Dunebound Tactics, a roguelite tactical RPG! 

[previewyoutube=v1YgHbn-ye8;full][/previewyoutube]

The game is in active development and we’ll be sharing regular updates on the progress here and on social media. We have a lot to show up until the release, such as the enemy factions, player classes and traits, as well as some behind the scenes stuff. 

Today though is a reason to celebrate and we would like to welcome you aboard for this journey, so wishlist and follow Dunebound Tactics for more in the coming future! 

Cheers!

Terahard Studios team
